title: Regional egress quiesce and operator handoff playbook
content:
Summary:
This document is a playbook for performing a controlled regional egress quiesce and staged traffic reroute into warm-standby capacity, plus the operator handoff checklist for long-running partial-region evacuations. It focuses on minimizing client impact, preserving KV-cache warm-state when possible, and clear rollback criteria. This is intentionally prescriptive (steps + exact operator communications) for on-call and incident commanders.

Scope and when to use this playbook:
- Use for partial- or full-region degradations where egress (outbound from the region to a set of external infra or public egress points) is saturated, intermittently failing, or causing unacceptable tail latency for inference requests.
- Not for single-service pod failures or simple autoscaling issues. For those, follow the standard SRE pod-level runbooks.
- Assumes warm-standby capacity exists in target region(s) and models are already provisioned. If not, follow the warm-standby provisioning checklist first.

Before you start (prereqs):
1) Incident lead and SRE on-call assigned; designate an operator to run the steps.
2) Verify warm-standby is healthy: per-route health checks green, model load success, GPU TSO stable.
3) Ensure rollback slack channel and on-call phone list are loaded; notify customer-success if customer-visible degradation expected.
4) Check KV cache pre-seed status (kv-preseed job): percent_warm > 60% preferred. If < 30%, expect cold-cache penalty and adjust shift cadence.
5) Ensure DNS change approval granted for TTL/weight updates if modifying records.
6) Open a tracking ticket (JIRA) and attach this playbook.

Telemetry and dashboards to watch (exact panels):
- per-region tail latency (P50/P90/P99) for text-generation and chat endpoints
- per-model QPS and GPU utilization on both source and target regions
- KV cache hit ratio and cache fill rate
- Route-level error rate (4xx/5xx split) and timeout counts
- BGP/edge egress health panel (if available): egress failure counts and ASN anomalies
- DNS propagation monitor (time-to-immutable) if using low TTLs

Alert thresholds (quick reference):
- Abort immediate cutover if P99 latency on target region > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Pause shift if request error rate increases > 4% absolute or > 2x relative for 5 minutes.
- Roll back if KV cache miss spike leads to sustained latency degradation beyond 10 minutes.

Pre-shift communication template (Slack + email):
- Channel: #sre-incident (post header)
- Message: "Incident SRE-####: starting staged regional egress quiesce from region-us-west-2 -> warm-standby eu-west-1. Expected client-visible impact: up to +150ms median for first 10 minutes due to cold KV cache; attempting 10% steps every 2 minutes. Point-of-contact: Maya Chen (pager). Tracking ticket: JIRA-SRE-837."

Stepwise staged traffic shift (recommended cadence):
1) Silence noisy non-critical alerts for routing adjustment (document silencing in ticket).
2) Set DNS TTL to 60s (if currently higher) at least 5 minutes before first weight change to reduce propagation lag.
3) Preseed KV cache where possible using /admin/kv-preseed - run 1x full pass for top 5k prefixes.
4) Begin shift: move 10% of traffic every 120s. Observe metrics for 3 minutes after each step.
   - Weights: 10 -> 20 -> 40 -> 60 -> 80 -> 100 (stop early if stable).
   - If any step triggers pause threshold, hold and let telemetry stabilize for 10 minutes.
5) When at 100% or the desired target weight: keep for at least 30 minutes of stability before any DNS TTL increase back to standard.

Operator commands and knobs (examples):
- Route53 weighted change (example): aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://change-weight-10pct.json
- Cloudflare TTL update: cf cli zones settings update --zone-id ZONE --record-id R1234 --ttl 60
- Router policy: update traffic-split policy in ingress-controller via k8s configmap: kubectl apply -f traffic-split-usw2-to-euw1.yaml
- KV preseed: curl -X POST https://admin.internal/kv/preseed?prefix=top-5k
(Operators: copy/paste these from the infra-runbooks repo to ensure correct hosted-zone ids and target names; hardcoded values in this doc are illustrative.)

KV cache considerations and mitigations:
- If preseed percent < 30% expect a cold-start latency penalty. Mitigation: slow cadence (5% steps every 3 minutes), enable increased batching timeouts in dedupe layer for 20 minutes.
- If we cannot preseed due to network constraints, plan for a gradual canary route with a fallback policy to model-fallback: small initial percentage only.

Rollback criteria and actions (blameless):
- Immediate rollback to previous weights if any of the following for 10 consecutive minutes: P99 > 2x baseline, 5xx > 1% and rising, or client-error spike tied to source region egress errors.
- To rollback: reverse the weight changes in the DNS/orchestrator to previous known-good values in a single step, confirm all health checks green, and then re-open an investigation ticket for deeper remediation.

Operator handoff checklist (for long-running evacuations where SRE is handing to on-call ops shift):
- Document current weight and exact timestamp for each routing change.
- Capture snapshot links to dashboards and take 1-2 screenshots of P99 and error-rate graphs.
- Save the KV preseed run id and percent_warm at handoff.
- List of active mitigations (silenced alerts, temporary autoscale overrides, increased logging).
- On-call person receiving handoff must ACK in #sre-incident and confirm they understand rollback criteria.
- Escalation path: on-call -> senior-sre (Priya Nair) -> engineering manager (Julian Rivera) -> infra-incident lead. Include phone numbers in ticket.

Post-shift monitoring and cleanup:
- Keep special telemetry dashboard pinned and increase sample rate for 60 minutes.
- Re-enable alerts that were silenced and note them in ticket.
- Revert DNS TTL to default only after 30 minutes of stability and then document propagation time observed.
- If the target region shows resource pressure after shift (GPU util > 85% for > 10 minutes), open a capacity scaling ticket and consider partial rollback.

Retrospective triggers (when to convert to a postmortem):
- Any customer-impacting errors noted during the shift.
- More than 30 minutes cumulative instability during the shift window.
- Any manual rollback required.
If any of the above, assign postmortem owner within 24 hours and link this playbook as an artifact.

Runbook maintenance notes (how this doc should evolve):
- After every execution, add a short execution note under 'edits' with date, operator initials, what worked, what didn't.
- If shift cadence is modified during execution, log the rationale and telemetry snapshot.
- Quarterly review with product-hosted-api to ensure customer-visible messaging templates are up to date.

Appendix: Quick reference (short bullets):
- Default step cadence: 10% every 2 minutes.
- Safe pause conditions: error rate > 4% abs or P99 > 2x baseline.
- KV cold-cache mitigation: preseed or step slower.
- Operator contact list: see ticket.

Known limitations and risks:
- DNS-based weight changes depend on edge caching; residual traffic to source region can persist for TTL duration.
- KV cache cannot always be fully pre-warmed across regions; expect transient RPS/latency spikes.
- BGP-level egress failures may cause asymmetric routing; validate with BGP panel before final cut.

Quick edit log (examples):
- 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: initial draft and checklist.
- 2025-02-21 Elliot Brooks: added KV preseed guidance and operator commands.
- 2025-03-01 Priya Nair: updated rollback thresholds and added handoff checklist.
